investigate: Middle school students often find it difficult to write arguments that are both ==structurally organised and scientifically credible==.
The study analysed ==supporting and opposing written arguments== from 109 eighth-grade students.
The arguments addressed three curriculum-aligned cases: nutrient cycling and plant vitality, thermal conductivity, and lightning formation.
find: Students relied mainly on ==referential evidence== and explicit scientific theory explanations.
==Supporting arguments were generally stronger== than opposing ones, which more often remained incomplete, weakly justified or low in credibility.
The study suggests students may need ==greater instructional attention== to justify claims, evaluate evidence and respond to alternative positions.

caption.question: How well do students argue for, and against, a scientific claim?
caption.intro: Filiz Bezci examines the **structural quality and scientific credibility** of supporting and opposing written arguments from 109 eighth-grade students across three curriculum-aligned science cases.
